name: Open ASR Leaderboard
ability_definition: The ability to identify and understand the speech of another person.

task_realism.reasoning: The audio comes from real speech sources that workers actually encounter: meetings (AMI), earnings calls, TED talks, parliamentary speeches and podcast-style GigaSpeech. That is closer to workplace listening than read-speech-only benchmarks. Still, some sets are prepared or read speech (LibriSpeech, much of TED and parliament). The task is passive transcription, not listening in order to act or respond in a live exchange.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is offline on pre-segmented utterances with no real-time or latency pressure. There is no interactive turn-taking, no chance to ask for clarification, and little surrounding situational context. Background noise, far-field audio and overlapping talk are only modestly represented; AMI is the main hard case. Real work involves live, noisy, multi-party, context-rich listening.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Word error rate captures the 'identify' half of the ability well but measures 'understand' only indirectly. There is no test of meaning, intent, speaker attribution or comprehension. Coverage is English-only with limited accent and dialect diversity. It excludes conversational phenomena such as crosstalk and diarization, and the short-form protocol omits long-form discourse tracking.

format_match.reasoning: Real audio in and text out is a genuine work artifact, since transcripts are produced in real jobs. However, human speech recognition at work usually yields understanding and action rather than a verbatim transcript. Scoring also strips casing and punctuation, which makes the output less like a usable document.

transferability_reasoning: The Open ASR Leaderboard uses authentic, varied real-world English speech and a natural audio-to-text format, so it transfers reasonably well for the identification component of speech recognition. Transfer is limited by offline, pre-segmented, non-interactive evaluation conditions. It is also limited by word error rate's inability to capture comprehension, so strong scores indicate accurate word recognition more than workplace understanding of speech.

2024.metric: average word error rate (%) across the leaderboard's English short-form test sets; lower is better
2024.human_reference: General adult workforce of fluent English listeners who must identify and understand others' speech at work. Non-specialist human transcription accuracy is used as the proxy.

2025.metric: average word error rate (%) across the English short-form datasets; lower is better
2025.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: people who must accurately identify spoken words in work settings, such as meetings, calls, lectures and dictation. Careful non-specialist listeners are the median, with professional transcribers as the upper end.

2026.model_or_system: ARK-ASR-3B (listed as Edge0/ARK-ASR-3B, a copy of AutoArk-AI/ARK-ASR-3B)
2026.metric: mean word error rate, % (lower is better)
2026.human_reference: General adult workforce: typical fluent English listeners who must identify spoken words in everyday work settings such as meetings, calls and speeches. Professional transcribers are used as an upper-end check.
